COMPACT_ANSWERS.1_why_little_visible_improvement_v6b_v6f: PASS measured feature/tab availability and persisted layout JSON (incl. PlaceOrder), not trading-free UX; V6F proved transient hide of right column only; reload restored full trading chrome — matches Owner visual experience.
COMPACT_ANSWERS.2_what_okx_native_can_do: Public WS: tickers, trades, books5; REST: candles, trades, mark, instruments; private GET plane spec for positions/orders/fills when WP-B activated — all server-side; not a persistent observation-only Safari layout.
COMPACT_ANSWERS.3_what_okx_native_cannot_do: Persistent hide order UI; parallel OB+T&S in one terminal panel; integrated ranking screener in WS2; durable observation layout across reload/Safari restart (evidence: V6F reload fail).
COMPACT_ANSWERS.4_architecture_fulfills_owner_goal: LOCAL_READ_ONLY_WORKSTATION (target) with HYBRID interim (Landscape + bookmarks, no layout hacks).
COMPACT_ANSWERS.5_required_data_sources: Mandatory: OKX EEA public WS+REST (market). Optional: WP-B private observation GET/WS (account panel). Optional: Peak CURRENT snapshots for ranking/selection/runtime/safety (non-authorizing, stale-labeled). Rejected/positive trades: UNKNOWN producer — fail-closed.
COMPACT_ANSWERS.6_security_risks: Mislabeling simulated Peak portfolio as OKX; browser-held API keys; adapter scope creep to POST; accidental orchestrator coupling; UNKNOWN endpoints default must FAIL_CLOSED.
COMPACT_ANSWERS.7_smallest_next_step: M0: Owner ratifies charter + M1 decision on WP-B vs exchange-blind bottom panel; freeze OKX Safari layout experiments permanently.
